title: Heterogeneous array, objects before the scalars - object elements silently deleted
rationale: The same shape as the previous fixture with element order reversed, and the damage is strictly worse: instead of a visible sentinel the object elements vanish and the output is a clean, plausible, wrong array. It exists solely because LinkedHashMap iteration order decides which of two colliding keys is written last.
catchesBugClass: Order-dependent silent data destruction from leaf/branch key collision. Also catches any change to MapFlattener fieldValues insertion order, which would flip this fixture to the sentinel-leak failure mode instead.
cannotCatch: It cannot detect the loss from the output alone - that is the point, and it means the harness must compare against the input, never self-validate the result. It also does not prove heterogeneous arrays fail in general, only in this collision shape.

predicted.detail: The one-segment key overwrites the array holder built from the longer keys, producing a syntactically perfect array with both object elements silently deleted and no error, warning, or log.
